title: Privatization and stock market liquidity
summary_en: Privatising state-owned enterprises by listing them on the stock exchange feeds new shares into the market — but does it actually improve overall stock-market liquidity? Boubakri, Cosset and Schindele use a cross-country panel of privatisation events to show that privatisation IPOs are associated with measurable improvements in domestic market liquidity, with effects largest in markets where pre-privatisation liquidity was thin. The paper documents one of the indirect benefits of privatisation programmes that is rarely captured in standard cost-benefit analyses.
data_used: Cross-country panel of privatisation IPO events with associated daily stock-market liquidity measures (turnover, bid–ask spread, Amihud illiquidity) over the post-privatisation window. Identification compares pre- vs. post-privatisation liquidity conditional on market and firm controls.
policy_relevance: Useful background for Hungarian state-asset disposal strategy (MNV, ÁKK, BÉT listing policy) and EU debates over re-privatising state stakes acquired during the COVID era. The liquidity-spillover argument supports IPO-based privatisation over private-sale auctions when the policy goal is to deepen domestic capital markets — directly relevant for any future MOL or Magyar Telekom-style large privatisation on the Budapest exchange.
